title: A Boy Appeared In A German Town Square In 1828. Nobody Ever Learned Where He Came From.
description:
In 1828, a teenage boy wandered into a Nuremberg square, barely able to speak. He claimed he'd spent his whole life locked in a dark cell. Nobody ever found out if that was true.

#shorts #truestory #unsolvedmystery
sources: Live Science's account of the Kaspar Hauser mystery
Mental Floss's coverage of Kaspar Hauser's life and death

scenes.text: On 26/05/1828, a teenage boy wandered into a public square in Nuremberg, Germany, barely able to speak and unable to walk properly.
He was carrying two letters. One asked a local army captain to take him in. The other, supposedly from his mother, said his father was dead and she could no longer care for him.
The boy said his name was Kaspar Hauser, and that he had spent his entire life alone in a dark, locked cell, only recently let out.
One of the letters turned out to be a forgery. It was addressed to a captain who wasn't even in the city the year it was supposedly written.
Some believed Hauser was a secret prince, hidden away to protect a royal bloodline. Others thought he'd invented the entire story.

In 1833, Hauser was found with a fatal stab wound, claiming a stranger had attacked him. Investigators at the time suspected he may have stabbed himself. Whether it was murder or a hoax gone wrong has never been settled.
